All integer, bit-exact vs a C golden model (score and id); 7.993 sustained / 8.000 peak dims/clock (P=8 roofline), 1-cycle fill/drain latency; 21.80x aggregate / 25.00x peak over a documented scalar cost-model baseline; 49 searches / 7364 vectors / 58912 beats per pass (9 directed corner cases - single vector, exactly-K, fewer-than-K, planted zero-distance hit, all-identical ties, IP argmax, IP ties, int8 saturation extremes - plus 40 randomised) checked bit-exact under randomised ingress bubbles and again at full rate, 762 result entries/pass, plus CSR statistics, a truncated-shard error/IRQ directed test, and full differential sim at D/P/K = 64/8/8, 32/4/4, 128/16/16, 256/16/8, 0 mismatches.

projects.name: gpu_kv_cache_paging_engine
projects.domain: memory management / paged KV-cache address translation for LLM serving (heterogeneous inference)
projects.microarchitecture: set-associative translation cache (SETS x WAYS parallel tag compare, true-LRU move-to-front order vector, invalid-way-first victim) + a block-table walker FSM + a LIFO physical-block allocator with a combinational stack-top read, all advancing on one bus-done gate so memory wait states stall the walk losslessly; the walker presents the next translation's key to the cache probe port while the current result word is on the bus, retiring one translation per bus transaction
projects.interface: Wishbone B4 classic single master over shared system memory (request array fetch, block-table read/write, result array writeback) + MMIO control/status register file with pool seeding, seven paging statistics counters and a sticky done / out-of-memory / bus-error interrupt cleared W1C
projects.software_layer: bare-metal C driver (configure, seed the block pool, submit a batch, wait on the interrupt, read paging statistics), a bit-exact golden model of the cache/LRU/allocator/block-table, a serving-trace workload generator, and a documented scalar cost-model baseline
projects.verification: Icarus Verilog SystemVerilog differential testbench with a Wishbone B4 slave memory model: two full passes over a 16-batch serving trace (randomised 0-3 memory wait states, then zero wait states) checking every result word (physical block AND flags), all seven statistics CSRs, FREE_COUNT/RES_WORDS, the sticky OOM bit and the IRQ, plus the entire 2048-word block table against the golden image; directed Wishbone ERR_I and never-acknowledged (watchdog) bus-error tests; mutation-checked (broken LRU victim and FIFO-instead-of-LIFO pool both fail); full differential simulation at 16x4/512, 8x2/256, 32x8/512 and 4x4/64 geometries
projects.summary: GPU/heterogeneous-inference KV-cache paging engine - the paged-attention (vLLM PagedAttention) block-table front end of an LLM serving stack: the attention kernels want physical KV-block numbers, the runtime thinks in (sequence, logical block) pairs, and this engine translates at bus rate while owning block allocation and release. A set-associative translation cache resolves a translation in one cycle (WAYS parallel tag compares, true-LRU move-to-front replacement, invalid-way-first victim); on a miss a block-table walker reads block_table[seq][idx] over Wishbone B4, fills the cache on a valid entry, and on an unmapped entry pops a physical block from a LIFO allocator, writes the entry back and reports ALLOC; OP_FREE walks a sequence's row, pushes each block back, invalidates its cache entry and poisons the entry, so the next allocation reuses blocks in LIFO order; OP_NOALLOC probes without growing, OP_FLUSH invalidates the cache, and an exhausted pool raises a sticky out-of-memory interrupt instead of evicting on its own (policy stays in software). Every state advances only on the bus-done gate, so wait states stretch the walk without changing a result, and the walker absorbs the next translation's key while the current result word is on the bus - 0.970 translations/clock peak (93.5% Wishbone occupancy), 3-cycle single-translation latency, 0.384 sustained translations/clock, 13.02x aggregate / 20.42x peak over a documented scalar cost-model baseline. Bit-exact against a C golden model over 16 batches / 371 request words / 1909 translations / 1955 result words per pass (directed: cold prefill, fully-cached re-read, flush-and-rewalk, NOALLOC on mapped and unmapped blocks, eviction + LIFO reuse, pool exhaustion mid-range, unknown opcode, both zero-count forms, host-populated rows, 9-way LRU thrash on one 4-way set, a 512-translation peak batch, plus 320 randomised requests) checked under randomised memory wait states and again at full rate, 8464 checks, including the whole 2048-word block table, plus CSR statistics, an out-of-memory IRQ, Wishbone ERR_I and bus-watchdog directed tests, and full differential simulation at 16x4/512, 8x2/256, 32x8/512, 4x4/64, 0 mismatches.

projects.name: gpu_embedding_gather_engine
projects.domain: recommendation inference / sharded embedding-table gather-reduce (DLRM / TorchRec multi-GPU EmbeddingBag)
projects.microarchitecture: double-buffered (ping-pong) row-staging pipeline: two CHUNKS x LANES x 32 staging buffers so the CHUNKS-beat memory burst of row i+1 overlaps the CHUNKS-cycle pooling fold of row i exactly, feeding LANES one-adder-deep reduce lanes (32-bit wrapping add for SUM/MEAN, signed compare-select for MAX/MIN, first-row init instead of a sentinel) into a CHUNKS-deep accumulator, with a divide-in-place MEAN pass through LANES 34-stage pipelined restoring dividers that needs no drain FIFO; CTRL.SINGLE_BUF collapses the overlap for a same-RTL A/B measurement
projects.interface: AXI4 burst read master (descriptor fetch, bag-index fetch, row gather; ARSIZE = LANES*4 bytes, INCR, AR beat presented the cycle the request is accepted) + AXI4 burst write master (pooled-vector scatter, W beats allowed to lag AW so the MEAN divider pass runs first) over shared device memory, driven by a host-built 8-word descriptor ring, plus a 19-register MMIO control/status plane carrying the shard window, seven pooling statistics counters and a sticky done / baglen / index / bus-error interrupt cleared W1C
projects.software_layer: bare-metal C firmware (descriptor-ring build from a batch of sparse features, shard-window and geometry configuration, device-ID bitstream check, start, interrupt service with W1C acknowledge, statistics readback for all-to-all sizing, and a host-side self-check), a bit-exact golden model of the classify/gather/pool/renormalise semantics, a workload generator, and a documented scalar cost-model baseline
projects.verification: Icarus Verilog SystemVerilog differential testbench with an AXI4 slave memory model: four full passes over a 319-bag ring (randomised 0-3 wait states on all five AXI channels, full rate, single-buffer mode, and a post-fault recovery run) checking every one of 20416 pooled output words against the golden image plus all seven statistics CSRs cross-checked against the beats the slave actually saw; the entire 41792-word descriptor/index/table region is compared against the pre-run image to prove the engine writes nothing outside the output region, and the output region is poisoned with 0xDEADC0DE so a missing write is a mismatch; 19 directed descriptors (empty bag, single local, single remote, all-remote, exactly LANES indices, MAX over INT32_MIN and -1, MIN over INT32_MAX and -1, SUM wrapping at INT32_MAX, MEAN truncating toward zero at -7/2, MEAN with count 1, MEAN exact, MEAN over alternating INT32_MAX/INT32_MIN, duplicate index five times, both shard boundaries, shard_hi classified remote, MAX_BAG-deep peak bag, num_idx > MAX_BAG rejection, index >= TABLE_ROWS, local+remote+invalid mixture) plus 300 randomised bags; directed read-SLVERR, AR-watchdog and zero-length-ring tests plus IRQ assert/W1C checks; mutation-checked (dropping the first-row accumulator init and renormalising MEAN by bag length instead of local count both fail); full differential simulation at EMB_DIM/LANES/MAX_BAG = 64/4/64, 32/8/32, 128/4/48, 32/2/64, 928256 checks, 0 mismatches
projects.summary: GPU/heterogeneous-inference sharded embedding gather-reduce engine - the nn.EmbeddingBag lookup path of a multi-GPU recommender (DLRM / TorchRec), where the sparse tower and not the dense one is the latency floor. Given a host-built ring of 8-word descriptors, each one a bag of row indices plus a pooling op, the engine fetches the descriptor, fetches the whole bag into a MAX_BAG-deep index buffer so the row gather never interleaves pointer loads with data loads, then classifies every index against this device's shard window [SHARD_LO, SHARD_HI): a local hit becomes one CHUNKS-beat AXI4 INCR burst, an index owned by a peer shard is skipped and counted in ST_REMOTE (which is what sizes the all-to-all that follows, so it is not an error), and only an index past the end of the global table raises a sticky error. The datapath is double buffered: row i+1 streams into one staging buffer while LANES one-adder-deep reduce lanes fold row i out of the other, one beat per clock, and because a row takes CHUNKS cycles to fold and CHUNKS beats to fetch the two stages are exactly matched - CTRL.SINGLE_BUF collapses the overlap in the same RTL and measures the gain at 1.667x. MEAN renormalises by the locally pooled count through LANES 34-stage pipelined restoring dividers writing quotients back in place, truncating toward zero exactly like C's /, so no drain FIFO is needed; an all-remote bag pools nothing and emits the zero vector the sharded reduce expects, and MAX/MIN are correct with no sentinel because the first locally pooled row initialises the accumulator. Every result is a function of the descriptor ring alone, never of bus timing or the buffering mode - 3.374 pooled words/clock peak (87.1% AXI occupancy, 18.97 cycles per 16-beat row), 2.917 sustained, 1.667x from double buffering, 13.17x aggregate / 14.08x peak over a documented scalar cost-model baseline. Bit-exact against a C golden model over 319 bags / 9523 indices / 6000 gathered rows / 384000 pooled embedding words / 20416 output words per pass (19 directed corner cases - empty bag, single local, single remote, all-remote, exactly LANES indices, MAX over INT32_MIN and -1, MIN over INT32_MAX and -1, SUM wrapping at INT32_MAX, MEAN truncating toward zero, MEAN count 1, MEAN exact, MEAN over alternating extremes, duplicate index five times, both shard boundaries, shard_hi as remote, a MAX_BAG-deep peak bag, num_idx > MAX_BAG rejection, index >= TABLE_ROWS, and a local+remote+invalid mixture - plus 300 randomised bags) checked under randomised AXI wait states, at full rate, in single-buffer mode and again after injected faults, 248960 checks per pass, including proof that nothing outside the output region is written, CSR statistics cross-checked against real bus beats, read-SLVERR / AR-watchdog / zero-length-ring / IRQ W1C directed tests, mutation checks, and full differential simulation at 64/4/64, 32/8/32, 128/4/48, 32/2/64, 928256 checks, 0 mismatches.

projects.name: gpu_kernel_dag_scheduler
projects.domain: heterogeneous runtime / multi-GPU kernel-DAG launch scheduling (CUDA-Graph command processor for heterogeneous inference)
projects.microarchitecture: associative dependency scoreboard: an on-chip graph CAM holding MAX_NODES x {dependency bitmask, device-affinity mask, duration, kernel id} whose masks are read out in parallel every tick, so all MAX_NODES readiness matches ((dep & ~done) == 0) resolve in one cycle; a combinational placer ANDs each ready node's affinity with the free-device mask and picks the winner through a two-level (group-of-8) priority encoder plus a device encoder, with fixed lowest-index tie-breaks; DEVICES countdown execution slots retire independently and in parallel, the retirement being registered so the done bit and the freed slot appear together on the next tick; the RUN phase touches no bus at all, so the schedule is a pure function of the graph, and nothing-runnable-with-nothing-running is an exact cycle detection rather than a timeout
projects.interface: AXI4-Lite control slave (18-register control/status plane: doorbell, node count, node/result base addresses, seven scheduling statistics counters, per-device occupancy, CAPS, and a sticky graph-done / error interrupt cleared W1C) plus a pipelined AXI4-Lite memory master (up to 4 outstanding addresses, AR running ahead of R, in-order returns so no reorder buffer is needed; AW and W held until both handshake, completion on B) reading a host-built node array and scattering one 4-word result record per kernel node
projects.software_layer: bare-metal C driver (graph construction in shared memory with an edge helper, device-affinity policy, launch doorbell, interrupt service with W1C acknowledge, per-node schedule readback and CSR collection, parallel-efficiency reporting for the next launch's rebalancing) plus a tick-by-tick golden model of the RUN phase and a software-only scheduler baseline that charges the CPU for every readiness scan visit, completion poll, launch and graph word load
projects.verification: 326 graph launches per pass (17 directed shapes + 9 directed rejection cases + 300 randomised DAGs generated in topological order then relabelled with a random permutation), 9991 kernel nodes, checked bit-exact against a C golden model on the per-node schedule and every CSR under randomised wait states on all five AXI4-Lite memory channels and again at full rate, 255388 checks per pass including a full 80844-word memory sweep proving nothing outside a result region is written, the two structural identities (makespan == dispatched + stall + depwait, sum(dev_busy) == serial_ticks), read/write SLVERR, fault recovery, IRQ masking and W1C tests, mutation-checked with three injected defects, and full differential simulation at 64x4, 32x2, 32x8 and 128x4 - 1113064 checks, 0 mismatches
projects.summary: A hardware command processor that launches a CUDA-Graph-shaped DAG of kernels onto the GPUs of a node by itself: an associative dependency scoreboard answers 'which kernels are runnable now' for all MAX_NODES at once, a combinational placer picks the lowest ready node and the lowest idle device its affinity mask allows, and DEVICES countdown slots retire in parallel so a dependent issues the cycle its last predecessor retires. 0.985 nodes/clock peak dispatch, 32-cycle single-graph latency, 2.583x parallel compression of 146263 serial ticks into 56632, 98.4% AXI4-Lite occupancy in the transfer phases, 17.62x aggregate / 18.37x peak over a documented scalar cost-model baseline.
